🧠 The Two Physical Intelligence Tests — For World Models (Video attached below: 🎥 Left: Genesis simulation, 🎥 Right: Real physical experiment) At first glance, the simulation looks perfect — the motion is smooth, the timing feels natural, and everything seems physically correct. But when placed side by side with reality, the differences become obvious. This simple comparison raises a deeper question: What does it really mean for AI to understand the physical world? In my view, we can think of this as two Physical Intelligence Tests, each measuring a different level of understanding. 1️⃣ The First Physical Intelligence Test — The Illusion of Realism This test measures perception — how well AI satisfies what the human eye expects. A model passes when: 1) Humans can’t tell real from synthetic, or 2)The brain’s neural response (for example, in fMRI activation patterns) to both is indistinguishable. Many models already achieve this level of visual realism in simple settings. But looking plausible is not the same as being physically correct. 2️⃣ The Second Physical Intelligence Test — The Understanding of Physics The deeper test is causal: Can an AI model generate worlds that not only look real — but also obey the laws of physics? To pass, a model must internalize the causal logic of reality — forces, friction, boundary conditions — and sustain an internal imagination of motion that remains consistent with those laws over time. Hand-crafted physics simulation alone won’t get us there. Even today’s best numerical solvers break down in complex, real-world scenarios — fluid dynamics, deformable materials, granular motion. True physical intelligence must therefore be data-driven, learned and validated directly from how the real world behaves, not just how we approximate it. A physically intelligent model doesn’t just depict reality — it predicts and respects it. 3️⃣ Why It Matters — Closing the Sim2Real Gap Much of today’s hype around video world models comes from their promise to train embodied agents — letting AI learn to act, plan, and reason through simulated experience. But the Sim2Real gap — where systems work in simulation but fail in the real world — persists because most models stop at the first test. They optimize for appearances, not causes. A video can look perfect while quietly breaking physics underneath. That’s why agents trained in such synthetic worlds often fail when faced with real materials, friction, or uncertainty. Closing that gap requires models that pass the second Physical Intelligence Test — those whose internal reasoning aligns with the causal structure of reality. Only then can AI-generated worlds become reliable foundations for embodied intelligence and real-world reasoning. The first test measures perception. The second measures understanding. AI will bridge the Sim2Real gap not when it looks real — but when it behaves real. #ArtificialIntelligence #PhysicsAI #WorldModels #Sim2Real #EmbodiedIntelligence ...more ...more

Thrilled to share that Allus AI (YC F25) is officially part of Y Combinator ’s Fall ’25 batch 🎉 The journey so far has been incredible, and we’re deeply grateful to be surrounded by such a supportive and inspiring community. Over the past few months, we’ve met some of the world’s leading manufacturers, moving between factory floors and cloud clusters while talking with customers nonstop. At YC, we’re more energized than ever, with new ideas and use cases emerging every day as we learn, build, and ship at YC speed. Huge thank-yous to TRACTIAN for believing in us early, with special thanks to Rafael Rejtman and Igor Marinelli for their support and encouragement, and to our mentors Rahul Saxena and Scott Mitchell for their valuable guidance at the very start of this journey. My cofounders Shijie and Zhisen have been building together for almost five years, and I’m incredibly proud of our team’s grit, focus, and persistence. As Paul Graham said, “Make something people want.” At Allus, we’re building the world’s first vision foundation model for manufacturing—a powerful model that delivers reliable, real-time quality inspection and process monitoring that scales seamlessly from edge to cloud. We’re also extending our model to help robotics companies automate their data labeling workflows. There are so many exciting use cases for this foundation model, and we’re just getting started. If you’re building factories of the future or working to automate your quality inspection or process monitoring, let’s connect. We’d love to learn from you and explore how we can help. ...more

Today, we’re launching Alpamayo 2 Super, our frontier open reasoning model for autonomous vehicles. Beyond seeing, Alpamayo understands and reasons through the complex world - thinks before it acts. It’s a powerful backbone for robotaxis, trucks, shuttles, delivery vans, tractors and the long tail of mobile robots—billions of autonomous machines someday. We’re releasing it for commercial use under OpenMDW-1.1 so teams can inspect it, fine-tune it and deploy it—open models advance safety and security. The next wave of AI is robotics—and it starts with autonomous vehicles. Great work, Alpamayo team! https://lnkd.in/g7urPEjp

Today, we're releasing our conversational speech model in public beta, and sharing our broader vision for Generalist Audio Models (GAMs): unified audio models that can follow complex instructions and learn from in-context examples. It has a Time-To-First-Audio (TTFA) of 300ms and is ready to plug into your voice agents. It’s a drop-in replacement for other TTS providers, but the part we're most excited about is that it adapt their tone based on the conversation history, so your voice agents are never tone-deaf. In blind human preference tests, raters chose our model over ElevenLabs Flash and Turbo on overall preference, naturalness, and quality, and it stays competitive with v3. The base model shows a wide range of capabilities: diverse audio generation, complex voice cloning, instruction-based steerability, and continuation of emotionally intense speech. This is our first step toward GAMs - unified audio models that outperform specialized models (TTS / STT / audio understanding / music generation) across a wide range of audio tasks, unlock new creative use cases, and give developers more control over how their speech models behave. A huge thank you to Andreessen Horowitz for having us at Finance Forum Demo Day at the New York Stock Exchange! The most forward-thinking finance teams aren't asking whether AI belongs in finance – they're hitting escape velocity with agents across close, operations, treasury, and more. For decades, finance organizations have wrestled with manual work across their stack, swiveling between ERPs, spreadsheets, financial management, and countless other systems. Brian Roberts captured it well: the promise of RPA was compelling, but it was difficult to get far on legacy tooling. The next generation of automation needs to be fast, reliable, and intelligent. With AI and computer-use today, we are there. Really enjoyed the conversations throughout the event. It’s exciting how many finance leaders are moving quickly and thoughtfully. CFOs aren't looking for AI for AI's sake; they're looking for technology to eliminate operational bottlenecks, improve reliability, and give their teams more leverage. Thanks to Ivan Makarov , Michael King , and the a16z team for hosting Sola at the NYSE ! The new era of finance is definitely an exciting one.
